items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: she found me a teacher whose name was Charles Bushman... 50 cents a lesson. The first lesson, he taught me the chromatic scale.

ctx.x: You just liked the look of it?

Yeah, I just liked the looks of it. I told my mother I wanted a saxophone. She said, 'well, I've spent money with you for piano lessons and you gave it up. Do you think you'll stick with this?' I said, 'Mama, get me a saxophone and I'll learn to play it.' And I wanted a C melody saxophone because, see, you didn't have to transpose, in those days. You could play from the piano sheet. So anyway, we were strong believers in Christmas and Santa Claus, you know. This Christmas, sure enough when I woke up Christmas…

chromatic scale. Well, that's all I needed. I went home and we had records all of these years and I started fooling around playing what those little things I had in my ear. And I started copying Coleman Hawkins who was the first saxophone player that I remember hearing. And he was recording with Fletcher Henderson's band in 1923. I remember when they picked him up and brought him -- Fletcher Henderson and Mamie Smith brought him out of St. Joseph, Missouri.
